questions.question: The passengers standing in a bus fall in the backward direction when the stationary bus begins to move. Which of the following laws explains this situation?

options.text: The Law of Conservation of Momentum

questions.solution:
• The passengers standing in a bus fall in the backward direction when the stationary bus begins to move due to the Newton’s First Law of Motion.
 
• The Newton’s First Law of Motion states that the body continues to be in rest or in motion in a straight line unless an external force act on it.
 
• It is also called as law of Inertia.
 
• According to the first law of motion as discussed above we can say when the bus is stationary then body continues to be in rest but when the bus begins to move, the body tends to move back to oppose the force caused due to the motion of the bus.

questions.question:
Find the value of the given expression.

6 – 36 × 3 ÷ 6 + 5 = ?
9800 Joules of energy was spent to raise a mass of 80 kg. The mass was raised to a height of______
questions.solution:
Given data

⇒ Amount of work done (E) = 9800 Joules or Newton-meter.

 

⇒ Mass of the object (m) = 80kg

⇒ Mass of an object raised to a height = h

⇒ Since the work is done against gravity, energy is stored in the object in the form of Potential Energy.

We know that potential energy(E) = m × g × h

⇒ h = E/(mg) where g is gravity and its value 9.81 m/s²

Now by substituting the above values in the above equation, we get

⇒ h = 9800/ (80 × 9.81) = 9800/784.8 = 12.4872 m.

We get h = 12.48 which is approximately equal to 12.5 meters.

Hence, The mass was raised to a height of h = 12.5 m

questions.question: A sphere is split in the ratio 1 : 3. The larger part is moulded into a cone having a height equal to the radius of its base, while the smaller part is moulded into a cylinder having a height equal to the radius of its base. What would be the ratio of the radius of the cone to the height of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the cone be ‘R’ and height be ‘H’ and radius of the cylinder be ‘r’ and height be ‘h’.

A sphere is split in the ratio 1 : 3,

⇒ Volume is also divided in the ratio of 1 ∶ 3.

The larger part is moulded into a cone having a height equal to the radius of its base, while the smaller part is moulded into a cylinder having a height equal to the radius of its base,

⇒ Volume of cone ∶ Volume of cylinder = 3 ∶ 1

⇒ 1/3πR³ ∶ πh³ = 3 ∶ 1

⇒ R³ ∶ h³ = 9 ∶ 1

∴ R ∶ h = sqrt[3]{9}:1

questions.question: An electric lamp of 100 W is used for 5 hours per day. How much energy will be consumed by the lamp for 3 days?
questions.solution:
Given data:

⇒ Rated value of the electric lamp (P) =100 watts

⇒ Amount of time the lamp is being used= 5 hours/day

⇒ The total amount of days = 3 days

⇒ The lamp is used for time (t)= 3 × 5

⇒ t = 15 h

We know that, Power(P) = E/t

Where ‘P’ is power in watts and ‘E’ is energy consumed in watt-hours and ‘t’ is time.

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

100 = E/15

E = 1500 Watt-Hours

E = 1.5 kWh or units. (1Kilo Watt Hour = 1 unit)

Hence, the energy consumed by the lamp in 3 days (E) = **1.5 kWh.**

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is/are true?

A. The 2ⁿd group elements are called Alkali metals.

B. The 1st group element is called Alkaline metals.

C. The 17th group elements are called Halogens.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Elements that have similar valance shell electronic configurations, the same number of electrons in their outer orbitals and has similar properties are divided into groups.
 
• The **2ⁿd group elements** are called **Alkaline Earth Metals**, have ns² outermost configuration and belong to the **s-Block Elements**.
 
• It contains elements from Beryllium (Be) to Radium (Ra).
 
• The **1st group elements** are called** Alkali Metals not **Alkaline, have ns¹ outermost configuration and belong to the **s-block Elements**.
 
• It contains elements from Lithium (Li) to Francium (Fr).
 
• The** 17th group elements** are called **Halogens **and have ns² np⁵ outermost configuration and belong to the** p-Block Elements**.
 
• It contains elements from Fluorine (Fl) to Ununseptium (Uus) / Tennessee (Ts).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/911546ce49b253295d6bad7533009add6219bf201c80ad73a569da76bce9f834.png]

• **The 2nd group elements are called Alkaline Earth metals, **not Alkali metals. Alkali metals are found in the 1st group.
 
• **The 1st group elements are called Alkali metals, not Alkaline metals.**
 
• **The elements in the 17th group of the periodic table are indeed called Halogens.**

questions.question: From each corner of a square with an edge of 4 cm, a 1 cm segment was chopped off from each side containing a vertex. What is the perimeter and the area of the octagon thus created?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4a4aedbee1c93d081d756c7a05a239aa2f09596e6a378cf3e3a2def9bdacea6.png] 

By cutting 1 cm off from each corner, each of the sides is now 2 cm, while each of the hypotenuse of the new edges is the hypotenuse of a right angle triangle with length, a = √2 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 2 + 4 × √2 = (8 + 4√2) cm

Area of octagon = Area of square – 4 × Area of right angle triangle

⇒ Area of octagon = 16 – 4 × 1/2 × 1 × 1 = 16 – 2 = 14 cm².

questions.question:
Consider the given argument and decide which of the given assumptions is (are) implicit.

**Argument:**

During the depression in the Bay of Bengal, the wind blew away all the hoardings.

**Assumptions:**

1. The wind was fast.

2. The hoardings were not fixed properly
questions.solution:
1:- **If the wind was strong enough to dislodge the hoardings:** Even if the hoardings were well secured, an extraordinarily strong wind could still blow them away.

 

2:-** If the hoardings were inadequately secured**: Even if the wind was not extremely strong, poorly secured hoardings could be blown away by a moderate wind.

 

Therefore, the argument depends on at least one of these conditions being met. Since either condition alone can lead to the conclusion, the correct interpretation is that at least one of these assumptions must hold true for the hoardings to be blown away during the depression.

Hence, Either wind was so fast that even properly fixed hoarding blew away or due to hoardings were not properly fixed, wind blew away all hoardings. So, either assumption 1 or 2 is implicit.

questions.question:
Consider the given statement and decide which of the given assumptions is (are) implicit m the statement.

**Statement:**

A person quoted, “Pride hath a fall”.

**Assumptions:**

1. Those who fall have pride.

2. Having pride can be counter-productive.
questions.solution:
The meaning of the statement is 'excessive pride would lead to mistakes and eventual failure'

In other words, having excessive pride is not a good thing.

Therefore, assumption 2 is implicit.

However, it cannot be assumed from the statement that those who fall (fail) have pride.

Hence, only assumption 2 is implicit.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 8% p.a is Rs. 90 more than simple interest at 9% p.a for 2 years on the same sum. The sum is (in rupees):
questions.solution:
Let the sum be 100x,

SI = sum × rate × time/100

The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 8% p.a,

⇒ SI = 100x × 3 × 8/100 = 24x

The simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 9% p.a,

⇒ SI = 100x × 2 × 9/100 = 18x

The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 8% p.a Is Rs. 90 more than simple interest at 9% p.a for 2 years on the same sum,

⇒ 6x = 90

⇒ x = 15

∴ Sum, 100x = Rs. 1500

questions.question: Mugdha and Mayuri, working together, can complete a job in 18 days. However, Mayuri works alone and leaves after completing two-fifths of the job and then Mugdha takes over and completes the remaining work by herself. As a result, the duo could complete the job in 39 days. How many days would Mugdha alone have taken to do the job if Mayuri worked faster than Mugdha?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Work done / Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the total work done by Mugdha and Mayuri = 90 unit

Efficiency of Mugdha + Mayuri = 90 / 18 = 5

Work done by Mayuri = (2/5) × 90 = 36 unit

Work done by Mugdha = 90 - 36 = 54 unit ​

Let the efficiency of Mayuri = x and Mugdha = y

Using concept,

⇒ 36 / x + 54 / y = 39 --- (1) 

As, Mayuri works faster than mughda.

So, only two cases that follow the above condition

Case 1: x = 3 and y = 2

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

A. The ratio of the force of gravitation between two masses, m1 and m2, kept at a distance R on the earth and on the moon is 1:1.

B. Nm²/kg² is the SI unit of G.

C. The value of G depends on the distance between the bodies.

D. The value of G depends on the masses of the bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**D and C.**__

__
 
• 
 
The ratio of the force of gravitation between two masses, ( m₁ ) and ( m₂ ), kept at a distance ( R ) on the earth and on the moon is 1:1. This statement is correct because the gravitational force (F = G m₁ m₂ / r²) depends only on the masses and the distance between them, not on the location (whether on Earth or the Moon). The value of the gravitational constant ( G ) remains the same regardless of where the masses are located. **Hence the statement A is correct.**

 
 
• The SI unit of Gravitational Constant (G) is N m²/kg². **Hence statement B is correct.**
 
• The Value of G is constant i.e 6.673 × 10–¹¹ N m² kg–².
 
 
• It does not depend on anything because it is constant. Its value remains the same everywhere as the value found out here ( Earth) should not vary anywhere in the universe. **Hence statements C and D are incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **​**The law of gravitation states that the force acting between two masses depends directly on the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance between them. It is given by :
 
 
• **F = G (m1, m2)/r2**
 
• G is the universal gravitational constant
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__** We have to find out the **incorrect** statements which are C and D.

questions.question: The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to twice the perimeter of a square. If a quarter of the numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square, then the length of one side of the square is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of edges of cube = 2 × Perimeter of square

Volume of cube = 4 × Area of square

**Concept Used:**

If the length of one edge of a cube be 'a' unit then volume = a³ cubic unit

Number of edges of a cube = 12

If one side of a square is 'a' unit then area of square = a² square unit

Perimeter = 4a units

**Calculation:**

Let the length of one edge of a cube = x and length of the side of a square be a,

The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to twice the perimeter of a square,

⇒ 12x = 2 × 4a

⇒ x = 2a/3

A quarter of the numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square,

⇒ x3/4 = a²

⇒ (8a³/27)/4 = a²

⇒ 8a³/27 = 4a²

⇒ a = 27/2 = 13.5 cm

**∴ Length of one side of the square is 13.5 cm**

questions.question:
What is the sum of the first 16 terms of the given series:

6, 13/2, 7, 15/2
questions.solution:
Series 6, 6.5, 7, 7.5,

Common difference, d = 0.5, first term, a = 6

⇒ Sum of first 16 terms = n/2[2a + (n – 1)d], where n is the number of terms

⇒ Sum of first 16 terms = 16/2[12 + 15 × 0.5] = 8 × 19.5 = 156

What is the percentage increase in the profit of Company X in 2016 with respect to that in 2014?

**Statements:**

1. Company profit in 2014 was Rs. 1 lakh, which is 10% more than that m 2015.

2. Company profit in 2016 was Rs. 2 lakh, which was Rs. 1 lakh more than that in 2014.

options.text: 1 alone is sufficient while 2 alone is not sufficient.
2 alone is sufficient while 1 alone is not sufficient.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Option 3. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Statement 1:

Company profit in 2014 was Rs. 1 lakh, which is 10% more than that m 2015,

Since we don't have any idea about the year 2016, so profit in year 2016 can-not be calculated.

Statement 2:

Company profit in 2016 was Rs. 2 lakh, which was Rs. 1 lakh more than that in 2014,

As we have a relation of profit in 2016 with respect to year 2014, so increase in profit percentage can be calculated.

Statement 2 alone is sufficient while statement 1 alone is not sufficient.

questions.question: If tan θ = 1/√5, find the value of cosec²θ – sec²θ.
questions.solution:
tan θ = 1/√5 = P/B

⇒ P = 1 and B = √5

⇒ H = √(P² + B²) = √6

⇒ cosecθ = H/P = √6

⇒ secθ = H/B = √6/√5

∴ cosec²θ – sec²θ = 6 – 6/5 = 24/5

questions.question: If 19th May 2012 was a Saturday, what day was 1st April 2014?
questions.solution:
Total number of days from19th May 2012 to 1st April 2014 = (12 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 + 1) = 682

Total number of odd days = 682/7 = 3 odd days.

So, Saturday + 3 = Tuesday.

Hence, 1st April 2014 was a Tuesday.

questions.question: A fraction when added to 7/3 gives 4. What is the fraction?
questions.solution:
Let the fraction be x/y, and when added to 7/3 gives 4,

⇒ x/y + 7/3 = 4

⇒ x/y = 4 – 7/3 = 5/3

∴ Fraction, x/y = 5/3
